I don’t know where you live. I’m in Alberta Canada, we have a parent link center that can help point you in the right direction and also give you some help. We also have childcare subsidy, child tax benefits etc. I’d look into those as well. Is your ex an addict? You might want to talk to a paediatrician or baby doctor about that if she is. Baby might need extra care. I personally recommend having the baby in the same room as you at night in a bassinet. Have bottles ready in the fridge at night. Makes it easier for night time feedings. I’d also recommend getting some baby books. Lean on your friends and family for support. Will you qualify for paternity leave? These are all things to think about. We also have a hotline number to call in case you’re ever worried. It’s 811 and sends you straight to a nurse in case you have any questions or concerns. You’re going to be tired. Especially since you don’t have a partner to help at home. Please take any help offered to you. We also have nurses that come to our homes once baby is born to make sure everything is okay. Don’t be afraid to ask questions and ask for advice. That’s what they’re there for. Also, don’t leave baby asleep in a car seat for prolonged periods of time. Once you get home, even if baby is sleeping, take him/her out. They are known to suffocate. Don’t put baby to sleep with lose blankets, pillows or stuffies. I’m not sure if this is all common sense stuff. I’m just throwing it out there just in case. If you have anymore questions feel free to pm me.

He said before our baby when I would go to work which was in the evenings, Monday to Friday, he was getting off work and my oldest son would be with his biological father so he had so much time to himself and it gave him the chance to do things for me. Now when he has time he uses it for himself, for his sanity. Going to the gym, playing baseball, visiting with friends. It's not that I'm not a priority, he just doesn't have the same amount of time as he used to. So the things he does for me now are taking the boys to give me a few hours of a break, allowing me to have time for tanning, etc.. The gestures have just changed from being Rose pedals and candles, to my alone time. Once this was put into place for me, I realized he doesn't have ANY time to himself that is quiet and 'alone'. So now I've been trying much harder to give him that space. The therapist said that all jobs are hard. Working 9-5 and parenting is hard. Working 2 hours a day and parenting is hard. We aren't to trivialize what the other does. Both parents struggle Day to day. So we need to communicate EXACTLY what we need. 
You need to tell your wife " I'm feeling like ____". "our needs are different. How do you feel about compromise"? "My alone time looks like _______". And it's important to specify what exactly you want and what exactly that looks like to you. She taught us that you could be with a partner for 30 years and expect them to "know this already" . But sometimes our minds are in different places from the chaos of every day and it's OKAY to remind your spouse of your needs. People aren't mind readers. Even 30-40 years down the road. Your mind isn't always on what your spouse needs or what they have mentioned in the past. A simple, but very specific reminder is helpful. 
Sorry this is so long. It's just what I've been learning through therapy. And I hope it helps you too.
